chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, and Bukayr, and Fudayl, and Burayd, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), among them being ones who reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and among them being ones who reported from one of the two (peace be upon them both).

That the woman does not inherit from the legacy of her husband from the dust of the house (land value) or land, except that the bricks and the wood would be valued, so she would be given her quarter, or her eighth if there was a child for her, from the value of the bricks, and the timber, and the canes.

key_terms.تُرْبَةِ دَارٍ: dust of the house (referring to land value)

ai.seo_question: How does a wife inherit from her husband's real estate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia juristic principle that a wife’s inheritance from real estate is limited to the value of the structures (turba) rather than the land itself, a distinction crucial for calculating shares in cases of partial inheritance. It specifies that her portion is one-quarter of the structure's value if there are no descendants, or one-eighth if there are, reflecting the interplay between fixed Quranic shares and specific asset valuation. This ruling highlights the scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between land and improvements when applying inheritance laws to property.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, and Bukeyr, and Fuzayl, and Bureyd, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, among them being ones who reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and among them being ones who reported from one of the two<sup>asws</sup>, that: ‘

The woman does not inherit from the legacy of her husband, from the dust of the house (land value), or land, except that the bricks and the wood would be valued, so she would be given her quarter, or her eighth if there was a child for her, from the value of the bricks, and the timber, and the canes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah, Bukayr, Fudayl, Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja‘far and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and certain ones of them has narrated from abu ‘ Abd Allah, and others have narrated who has narrated the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘

A woman does not inherit from the legacy of her husband in the form of land of his house or land. However, she can inherit from bricks and wood which must be appraised from the value of which one-fourth must be given to her or one-eighth, if she has children, of the value of bricks, branches and wood.’”
